title: Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation (various directions)
description:
[Looking for undergraduate or master's students to join in the fall and beyond]

We are building bimanual dexterous manipulation systems that perform useful tasks with human-like robotic hands. Relevant background works include [Cloak](https://tml.stanford.edu/cloak/): our cross-embodiment training recipe for zero-shot manipulation with unseen embodiments, [SPD](https://spd.bot/): work from our lab that pre-trains dexterous policies on VR-teleoperated simulation data and fine-tunes them on a bimanual robot, and [ABC](https://abc.bot/): an open-source stack for large-scale behavior cloning. Building on this, we are interested in several potential research directions, including post-training recipes (e.g. DAgger, real2sim2real RL), multimodal reasoning (e.g. tactile), in-context learning (e.g. memory), and data collection devices. This posting is not tied to any specific one of these; we will define a project together based on your background and the direction you find most compelling.

Outcomes:

- **Authorship.** Ownership of a project with first or co-first authorship on submissions to top venues (e.g., CoRL, RSS, NeurIPS).
- **Mentorship.** Close, hands-on guidance through the full research cycle, with the potential for continued collaboration beyond the initial project.

Criteria:

- **Time.** Substantial time commitment during the fall quarter (and potentially beyond). Please be candid about your availability and other commitments.
- **Length of Collaboration.** Desire to stay with the lab for longer than 1 quarter. We value building lasting connections and long-term mentorship. This is not a commitment (for either party), but a soft intention.
- **Experience.** One or more of the following are good to mention: Publications in robot learning, relevant internship projects, relevant coursework with a significant project component, or another experience you believe is relevant.

In your application, please describe your relevant experience and which research directions interest you.
